app.run:
The app is Funkuino Studio, a localhost web app (aiohttp server + vanilla-JS frontend). Never run it against the owner's real library (~/Music/Funkuino) or the real ESPuino box: a click on Sync would write to a device a child may be listening to. Instead start it against a throwaway library, without a device, on a free port, from the workspace root (needs the setup's .venv):

```
D=/tmp/funkuino-obeya-$(basename "$PWD"); mkdir -p "$D"
.venv/bin/python -c 'import sys; from pathlib import Path; sys.path.insert(0, "dev"); import shot; shot.seed_library(Path(sys.argv[1]))' "$D/library"
PORT=$(.venv/bin/python -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(); s.bind(("127.0.0.1",0)); print(s.getsockname()[1])')
FUNKUINO_CONFIG_DIR="$D/config" FUNKUINO_DATA_DIR="$D/library" PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 nohup bin/funkuino studio --no-browser --port "$PORT" --host funkuino-demo.invalid > "$D/studio.log" 2>&1 &
echo $! > "$D/studio.pid"; echo "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" > "$D/url"
```

The address is then in `$D/url`, the server log in `$D/studio.log`. The seed (dev/shot.py's `seed_library`) makes one song, one Hörspiel and one album with covers, so the Bibliothek tab has rows to show; put more files under `$D/library/files/` and `$D/library/card-covers/` (naming conventions in CLAUDE.md) to show other states. There is no login. The device is unreachable on purpose, so Studio shows the box as offline and Sync/RFID cannot touch hardware; the Agent tab is not set up (scratch config dir, no token), which costs nothing. If a change can only be shown with the real box or the agent, ask the owner first. After a change to the frontend (scripts/studio_web/) reload the page; after a Python change stop and start the server again. For a quick look without a browser, `.venv/bin/python dev/shot.py [bibliothek|agent|sync|karten]` writes screenshots to dev/shots/. Stop the server afterwards by its PID: `kill $(cat "$D/studio.pid")`.
app.stop: D=/tmp/funkuino-obeya-$(basename "$PWD"); if [ -f "$D/studio.pid" ]; then kill "$(cat "$D/studio.pid")" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$D/studio.pid"; fi; true
